text:
maya: Heads-up — planning a DR failover test from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 next week. I want to validate AWS KMS multi-region replica behavior, cross-account access for DR (we may run replica in a secondary account), and envelope encryption/key rotation implications. Quick questions: can a replica KMS decrypt ciphertext created by the primary? Can we create replica keys cross-account? What do we need for safe key rotation during failover?

cj: Short answers up front: 1) Yes — multi-Region keys are intended so replicas can decrypt ciphertext created by the primary (if configured as a multi-Region key). 2) You can create replicas in another account/region but you must set that up while primary is available. 3) For rotation, prefer rotating data keys and rewrapping envelopes; plan re-encrypt jobs.

olivia: From our last DR run notes: ciphertexts include the key ARN and MRK metadata, so app logic needs to map local region -> local replica ARN to avoid unnecessary cross-region KMS calls. If you failover, update the mapping to point to the replica ARN. Also store envelope metadata with object (key_arn, key_version, region).

saul: Important nuance on rotation: automatic CMK rotation (enable-key-rotation) changes KMS key material, but it doesn't magically rewrap all existing data keys. If you want all envelopes to be encrypted under a newer CMK version you must re-encrypt (re-wrap) the envelope keys using Rekey/ReEncrypt flows or generate new data keys and rewrite objects. We usually: generate new data key, decrypt object with old data key, encrypt with new data key, and then encrypt new data key with local CMK. Use KMS ReEncrypt API for bulk rewrap where possible.

maya: Example for doing temporary cross-account access during a DR run — is a grant better than modifying key policy?

olivia: For short-lived DR runs grants are handy because they can be created and retired programmatically. Example CLI grant (create on the target replica key):

```
aws kms create-grant \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444455556666:key/replica-key-id \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/DRRunRole \
  --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey ReEncryptFrom ReEncryptTo \
  --name "dr-run-grant"
```

olivia: If you're going cross-account for the replica itself, key policies must allow the principal creating the replica and the target account principals. Replication is created from the primary side, and you need to authorize the replica creation in the other account.

cj: Grants are tied to a specific key (and region). So if you create a grant on the replica key in us-west-2, that only controls the replica. Key policy changes are global to the CMK logical key (but note each replica has its own key ARN). For persistent cross-account trust prefer a key policy + IAM role approach; for temporary access use grants.

saul: Failover checklist (short):
- Pre-create replica MRKs in target region(s) and verify status.
- Pre-create IAM roles / trust relationship in target account and test AssumeRole flows.
- Provision grant templates (CLI step above) and script grant creation/removal as part of DR.
- Add region-aware key ARN mapping in config and a small cutover script to switch mapping.
- Run end-to-end decrypt tests before cutover (object decrypt + auth audit).
- Run background rewrap job for envelope keys if rotating envelopes as part of cutover.

maya: One more: if primary is in account A and we want replica in account B — are there limits or gotchas?

olivia: You can replicate to another account but replication creation requires the primary to authorize the replica. So you must create the replica while you still have access to primary (not during outage). Also double-check: cross-account replication requires specific key policy entries and potentially KMS service principals. We should follow the AWS guide: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/multi-region-keys.html

cj: Audit / monitoring notes: KMS CloudTrail events are regional. For post-incident forensics, centralize CloudTrail ingest (S3 bucket + Athena) across regions and ensure KMS API events are included. Also add metric alarms on kms:Decrypt counts for unusual spikes.

saul: Practical rewrap pattern we use: keep key_id + region + key_version in envelope metadata. When we rotate envelopes, spawn a bounded concurrency job that reads objects, calls GenerateDataKey (or Decrypt old data key via KMS), re-encrypts payload, then calls GenerateDataKey+Encrypt to create new envelope. Use DynamoDB or SQS to track progress and retries.

maya: Great — action items from this thread: 1) create us-west-2 replica MRK for account 444455556666 while primary healthy, 2) prepare IAM role + grant template for DR-run, 3) add key ARN mapping + smoke tests to run in DR rehearsal, 4) schedule background rewrap job (non-blocking). Assigning to @cj and @olivia to get templates together by EOD Fri. :thumbsup:
